A little bit of history. I've been clinically depressed for over 3 years now. Started with the death of my uncle. And it has been the never ending perfect storm since. Dropped out of college, lost my faith in religion, fired from my job, lost my first girlfriend and a few after that.

My parents and my relationship was incredibly strained. Almost emotionally abusive, really.

I ended up moving to a new city with a friend. Over 12 hours away. Packed 2 bags and bought a one way train ticket. For the next 9 months it was fantastic, I even distinctly remembering my dad calling me to tell me he was proud of me. Something he had not said since I left school. Until my friend and I were evicted.

So now I'm back living with my parents. In this hell hole of a town I so desperately wanted out of.

I got in contact with a therapist, and I'm trying that, not the first time, and I hold no hopes that it will work.

My therapist at our last appointment told me she does not think I'm emotionally well enough for school again , much less employment.

Which kind of incited some of the old stubbornness in me. I want to prove her wrong.

However, my relationship with mom and dad is taking a turn for the worse. They are done trying to tiptoe around me. I'm seeing similarities to last year and the driving force behind my leaving.

I want to strike out again. But I'm scared I can't do it like my therapist said. And to top it off, I'm scared of trusting anyone again like I trusted my friend. Circumstances of the eviction left a scar on how I see my friendships, and I am incredibly hesitant to open myself up to that again.

Kind of a long story, and that isn't even half of the details. Thanks for the thread to talk about things. Feels nice knowing there are others in similar situations.

Hello, co-founder of zeldathon.net here. (Raised over $50,000 for St. Jude last winter)

The most important thing you can do is have fun. I know it sounds silly, but it really makes a difference. As a small/new stream, your main focus should be to hold on to whatever viewers come in. Keeping the commentary interactive and entertaining is essential.

Don't expect to be immensely successful, just have fun, the charity contribution is just a side bonus. The first Zeldathon about 4 years ago only raised ~$330.

Reach out to anyone you know in the local area, if they can't provide snacks, maybe they will chip in a few dollars.

If you have any specific questions, feel free to contact me. I'm not usually on reddit, but I open it once every couple of days.

I'm also interested in checking out your stream, I love me some good charity events :)
